goals.0: Asking and telling the time: „Wie spät ist es?“
goals.1: Viertel nach / vor and halb — quarter past, quarter to, half past
goals.2: „halb vier“ = 3:30 — the biggest trap in German!
dialog.0.de.2.n: wie spät = literally “how late” — it means “what time is it?”
dialog.1.de.3.n: Uhr = clock; after a time it means “o'clock”
dialog.4.de.4.n: halb vier = 3:30 — “half before four”! You name the next hour
dialog.4.de.5.n: halb vier ≠ 4:30. Half past three = halb vier
dialog.5.de.2.n: Being on time is very important in Germany
grammar.0.title: Hours and minutes (everyday speech)
grammar.1.title: The biggest trap: halb
grammar.1.text: „halb vier“ does not mean 4:30, it means 3:30 — “half an hour before four”. In German the number after halb is the next hour. So halb drei = 2:30 and halb acht = 7:30. English “half past three” and German „halb vier“ are the same time.
grammar.2.title: Official / 24-hour time
grammar.2.text: Train and bus timetables, doctors and offices use the 24-hour clock: 15:30 = fünfzehn Uhr dreißig, 18:45 = achtzehn Uhr fünfundvierzig. There is no halb/Viertel here — just hours and minutes. Question: „Wie spät ist es?“ or „Wie viel Uhr ist es?“
quiz.2.why: Viertel vor drei = 15 minutes before three = 2:45.
quiz.4.why: fünf vor acht = 5 minutes before eight = 7:55.
